alt: KBo 44.52 and the five steps of the method, ending in its placement with the Syro-Mesopotamian (Hurrian) rituals
title: From fragment to tradition
caption: The method in five steps, on the orphan KBo 44.52 (CTH 470).
credit: Photograph: Hethitologie-Archiv Mainz, hethiter.net/: fotarch N06460 (KBo 44.52). Text: TLHdig Beta 0.3.

alt: KBo 44.52: the photograph and its transliteration; restored signs grey
title: 1 · Read
caption: Only what is visible on the tablet counts: 49 of the 53 words of the edition. A word counts if at least half its signs are preserved, or if it is preserved elsewhere on the same tablet.
credit: Photograph: Hethitologie-Archiv Mainz, hethiter.net/: fotarch N06460 (KBo 44.52). Text: TLHdig Beta 0.3.

alt: Weights of words in KBo 44.52: rare words such as LÚSIMUG weigh much, the common sign nu little
title: 2 · Count
caption: Every word form and every sign sequence inside a word gets a weight: high if it is rare in the other manuscripts, low if every text has it.
credit: Photograph: Hethitologie-Archiv Mainz, hethiter.net/: fotarch N06460 (KBo 44.52). Text: TLHdig Beta 0.3.

alt: Similarity of KBo 44.52 to the ten traditions; Syro-Mesopotamia (Hurrian) is nearest
title: 3 · Compare
caption: Each tradition is the average profile of its manuscripts. The fragment is compared with each of the ten: 1 means identical, 0 nothing shared.
credit: Photograph: Hethitologie-Archiv Mainz, hethiter.net/: fotarch N06460 (KBo 44.52). Text: TLHdig Beta 0.3.

alt: The lead of Syro-Mesopotamia (Hurrian) over the Kizzuwatna rituals, 0.115, against the 0.028 needed
title: 4 · Decide
caption: A fragment is placed only when the nearest tradition leads the runner-up by at least 0.028, the margin at which 8 of 10 test fragments of known tradition land correctly. Below it the answer is "undecided".

alt: The words that decide the placement of KBo 44.52, and its closest manuscript KBo 59.165 (CTH 701), side by side
title: 5 · Explain
caption: Every placement comes with the words it rests on, and with the closest manuscripts and compositions to read next to it. Here: KBo 59.165 (CTH 701), 17 shared words, 5 shared phrases; closest composition CTH 701, Drink offering for the throne of Ḫebat.
credit: Photographs: Hethitologie-Archiv Mainz, hethiter.net/: fotarch N06460 (KBo 44.52), fotarch B1358b (KBo 59.165). Text: TLHdig Beta 0.3.
